units.passage: As we integrate AI into our classrooms, it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges, ensuring that our use of this technology remains both responsible and grounded in the real needs of our learners.
units.why: 'it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges' asks users to balance gains and risks before using AI; P118.

units.passage: Be thoughtful about when this tool is useful. Don’t use it if it isn’t appropriate for the case or circumstance.
units.why: "Don't use it if it isn't appropriate for the case or circumstance" asks students to judge fit before using AI, P118.

units.passage: understanding of AI, you can guide your tools to produce accurate and relevant responses. View Prompt Tips General Principles for AI Use at UNF The University of North Florida establishes the following guiding principles for the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools by our community. We base these principles on our core values as articulated in our strategic plan. These principles will be further codified and articulated in relevant policy documents for faculty, staff and students. These principles will also guide how we work with AI and our partners in the northeast Florida region. In using AI, UNF faculty, staff and students will... Understand that AI is a tool and as such has its uses, strengths, limitations and risks.
units.why: "Understand that AI is a tool and as such has its uses, strengths, limitations and risks" asks users to understand AI limits, closest to P118 (weigh benefits and risks).
units.fit_note: Asks for understanding of uses and risks, not an explicit decision about whether to use AI. / Asks users to understand AI as a tool with strengths and risks; no instruction to weigh before use.

units.passage: Surfacing and examining your values and assumptions with careful reflection helps you to be intentional about choosing appropriate commitments.
units.why: "Surfacing and examining your values and assumptions with careful reflection helps you to be intentional" asks instructors to weigh their own values before choosing AI commitments; P118 (weigh benefits, risks and values) fits, though it is addressed to instructors rather than users in general.
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors choosing course commitments, not to users deciding whether to use AI.

units.passage: the importance of considering the normative questions—the ‘whether’ and ‘if so, how’ questions—that attend use of these tools.
units.why: The Committee recognized "the importance of considering the normative questions", the whether and if-so-how questions about using these tools. It asks users to weigh values before use (P118), so should, with a neutral unit stance.
units.fit_note: Frames whether and how to use AI as normative questions to examine; does not tell users to weigh benefits and risks.

units.passage: also encourages its community to consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI.
units.why: "consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI" asks the community to weigh benefits and harms of using AI in context, so P118 with "should" (encourages).

units.passage: AI use also elicits a number of social, legal, and ethical questions for education, research, and the workplace worthy of consideration.
units.policy: AI use raises social, legal, and ethical questions for education, research, and the workplace that are worthy of consideration.
units.why: The text notes AI "elicits a number of social, legal, and ethical questions for education, research, and the workplace worthy of consideration"; users are asked to weigh ethics and risks, P118.

units.passage: When it comes to GenAI, we want to help you: understand how GenAI output is created and how to use it to generate text, learn how to evaluate how well GenAI output meets the context-specific needs of particular writing situations, and make informed decisions about when and how to use GenAI–and how doing so may benefit or harm yourself or others.
units.why: The Writing Center says it wants to help students 'make informed decisions about when and how to use GenAI' and how it may 'benefit or harm yourself or others': weighing benefits and harms, P118.
units.fit_note: Stated as a Writing Center service goal rather than a student duty.

units.passage: Make intentional choices about when and how to engage with AI
units.why: 'Make intentional choices about when and how to engage with AI' asks students to decide deliberately whether to use AI. P118 (weigh benefits, risks, values) is nearest.
units.fit_note: Intentional choice, but benefits and risks are not named.

units.passage: Keep in mind that an approved tool is not the whole answer: whether a use of AI is appropriate also depends on the data you put in, what the AI is being used to do or decide, and any law, regulation, or contract that applies to your work.
units.why: Asks users to judge appropriateness by data, purpose and law, not tool approval alone: weighing context before use, P118.
units.fit_note: Context factors are data, purpose and law, not benefits and values.

units.passage: Stay informed about the ethical concerns surrounding generative AI so that you can make an informed decision about whether to use it.
units.why: 'Stay informed about the ethical concerns... so that you can make an informed decision about whether to use it' asks students to weigh ethics before deciding to use AI; P118 fits better than P102 because the stated purpose is the decision whether to use.
units.fit_note: Also a duty to stay informed (P102).

units.passage: AI-generated content, including deepfakes and synthetic media, can be used maliciously to deceive, manipulate, or harm individuals. Faculty, students, and staff should be cautious when engaging with AI-generated content and should report any suspected misuse to the Office of Information Security.
units.why: "Faculty, students, and staff should be cautious when engaging with AI-generated content" because it "can be used maliciously to deceive, manipulate, or harm"; it asks users to be careful and weigh risk, so P118, should.
units.fit_note: Caution about deepfakes and synthetic media, not a weighing of benefits and risks before choosing to use AI.

units.passage: The CTLE advises faculty to reflect on the ethical considerations of using Gen AI both in and outside of the classroom.
units.why: "The CTLE advises faculty to reflect on the ethical considerations of using Gen AI both in and outside of the classroom" asks faculty to weigh ethics before use, so P118.

units.passage: We explore new AI tools boldly while weighing benefits against risks.
units.why: Principle 2: 'We explore new AI tools boldly while weighing benefits against risks' (P118).
units.fit_note: Also encourages bold exploration, not only weighing.

units.passage: However, it also poses considerable dangers for those who venture into the realm of Generative AI without a comprehensive grasp of the associated risks.
units.why: The opening says GenAI offers prospects for those who use it 'creatively, responsibly and ethically' but poses 'considerable dangers' without understanding the risks; this weighs benefits and risks before use, so P118.
